anchor_means: per index and read: float64 vectors summed in the anchor bank's file order, then divided by the count
cosine: torch.nn.functional.cosine_similarity(v, mean, dim=0) on float64 CPU vectors
cuda: untested on CUDA; checked on CPU fixtures only

datashield.cas: cas_i = v_i' S_inter v_i / v_i' (S_inter + S_intra) v_i on the anchors' read (b) states z-scored per dimension over both classes (population SD; SD 0 gives 0); classes harmful and safe; sums of squared projections (SPEC 4.1 Eq. 3-5 as written)
datashield.css: css_i = (read c - read d) . v_hat_i, per row and index
datashield.direction: v_i = harmful anchors' mean of read (c) - safe anchors' mean of read (c); v_hat_i = v_i / ||v_i||

family_78b.engine_rule: PP4 (the lead's ruling, 5 Nov 2026): every wrapper kind runs on engine X (engine_x above): untuned_answers, rep_pass, l1_scan and classifier on the pod; l1_score, s3_score, score_edit, add_edit and s_pool on the Mac. Every derived settings file carries engine_x unchanged from the 1B file, and the frozen check_settings refuses another engine identity (R: scripts/stage1/s1common.py:589-591). A run on engine Y needs the settings re-derived for Y (engine_x = Y's identity, a new PINS-78B.json, a new PINS_FILE_SHA256) by a recorded step; none exists. The engine's own jobs (the a0-1101 retrain, a1_pass) follow ruling 10 and addendum A13, not this rule. The kit packs scorer pods with engine X.
family_78b.rule: the 1B file's schema and name, so scripts/stage1's unchanged check_settings accepts it; every value that differs from the 1B file is per family (pins_78b.json) or a documented 7-8B rule; a null is a pin that waits for the event named in waits; scorers_78b.py refuses a command while a pin it needs is null

pins.anchor_bank_sha256.event: the Llama-3.1-8B anchor job (scripts/make_anchor_answers.py on the family's main recipe, single-job pod, KD6): anchors.sealed.json 'anchor_file_sha256' of its committed record

pins.recipe_sha256.event: the Llama-3.1-8B anchor job, then scripts/scale78b/make_recipe_s78.py --family llama31-8b --anchors-sha256 <anchor_file_sha256>, then the lead's commit by explicit path (addendum A1, A2); the same value as runkit/stage1-78b/rules_78b.py RECIPE_S['llama31-8b']

gate_c_reproduction: at (index n, read b): per unit, fsum / count of cos_harmful, cos_safe and their difference; equal byte for byte (canonical JSON) to the pinned scripts/gate_c_representation.py groups block (998231ea), checked on a CPU fixture
index_convention: index 0 = the embedding output; index i (1 <= i <= n - 1) = the raw output of block i - 1; index n = model.norm(the output of block n - 1); block b's output is index b + 1, post-final-norm for b = n - 1 (transformers 4.56.2 exposes no raw output of the last block)
model_agnostic: the layer count n, the hidden size and the final norm are read from the loaded model (config.num_hidden_layers, config.hidden_size, get_decoder().norm); a 7-8B run gets its own settings file
name: representation_pass
pools: optional stage-1 text pool files ({kind, version 1, name, items: [{id, prompt, response}]}) named by SHA-256 on the command line; each item encoded by encode_train under the recipe's max_train_tokens; a refused item is counted by reason and not scored

reads.a: position L - 1: the end-of-turn token (the row must end with codec.eos_id)
reads.b: position L - 2: the last response token (the pinned Gate C read)
reads.c: the mean over the response tokens, positions n_prompt .. L - 2 (end-of-turn excluded)
reads.d: position n_prompt - 1: the last templated-prompt token (the end of the assistant header)

requirement: REQ-3 (brief rev 1, RS B1, SPEC section 8; lead decisions L3, L4; the lead's Part C model-agnostic requirement); 7-8B: Part 1 section 12 (the rep_pass kind, REQ-3's pass for L1 and S3), section 14 item 1
roles: L1's arm uses only (index l_s + 1, read a); S3 uses read (a) at indices 1..n; DataShield-style uses css and cas at indices 1..n; Gate C's reproduction uses (index n, read b); every other (index, read) cell is report only and never selects rows or defines an arm (L3 (1))
